baseline.note: Run 28 is the baseline audit. Counts are samples; this ledger is the source of truth.

findings.claim: The missing-review-target validation is re-established only on the inline branch (and there only for explicitly prefixed paths); the `--driver prompt` / host-without-child-sessions branch and the engine path's repo-relative typo check are not applied to the prompt route.
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts
findings.reason: Explicit path targets are validated on the prompt path as well as the inline path.

findings.claim: The shared index-plan adapter treats any 0-based decision subset whose indices start at 1 as 1-based and shifts it, applying the synthesizer's merge/rank decisions to the wrong findings.
findings.test: test/engine.test.ts::a contiguous subset without index 0 stays zero-based
findings.reason: Only a full 1-based plan is shifted; a compliant 0-based subset is no longer applied to its neighbors.

findings.claim: The grouped-verdict text fallback only shifts a contiguous 1-based list, so a sparse 1-based verdict list is mapped onto the wrong candidates and the rest are dropped.
findings.test: test/json.test.ts::asGroupVerdicts shifts 1-based lists, including partial ones, but not after index 0 was dropped
findings.reason: A sparse 1-based verdict list is shifted as a unit instead of dropping out-of-range entries and misattaching the rest.

findings.claim: The fallback permission table used when `ctx.agent.transform` is unavailable grants no shell action, even though every prompt tells the agent to run git commands when the diff is truncated.
findings.test: test/prompts.test.ts::the three review agents share one read-only policy module
findings.reason: The Markdown fallback now allows the exact diff command the prompt displays, so a truncated diff can still be inspected without agent.transform.

findings.claim: The shell deny rules match control characters anywhere in the command string, including inside the sanctioned, quoted diff command, so a review of a path whose name contains `&`/`;`/`>`/`|` is blocked even when the child runs exactly the command the prompt displays.
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts::a path with a shell metacharacter omits the pathspec from the runnable command
findings.reason: A path containing a denied shell character omits the pathspec from the runnable command; the captured diff stays scoped.

findings.claim: An explicit-range review treats a failed `git diff --quiet HEAD` worktree probe as clean and silently reviews only committed changes.
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts::a failed worktree probe in an explicit range is an error
findings.reason: Exit >1 from git diff --quiet is a discovery failure, not a clean worktree.

findings.claim: The same-branch check never strips a remote prefix, so targeting `origin/<current-branch>` omits uncommitted changes.
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts::a remote-prefixed current branch includes uncommitted changes
findings.reason: A remote-tracking target is matched to the checked-out branch through real remote names.

findings.claim: A conventions file that is fully read but longer than its character budget is truncated without the `…(truncated)` marker, so the prompt silently omits rules.
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts::a fully read conventions file over the character budget carries the truncation marker
findings.reason: A fully read file cut by the character budget now carries the truncation marker.

findings.claim: A path or path-hinted review never records the checked-out branch, so `--comment` is refused even when the anchors are in the PR diff.
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts::a clean path target records the checked-out branch
findings.reason: Clean path and free-form reviews record the current branch so --comment can resolve the PR.

findings.claim: The documented fallback for a PR response without a `url` asks `gh pr view --json baseRepository`, a field `gh pr view` does not support, so the base-repository fallback can never succeed and `--comment` aborts instead of resolving the repository.
findings.test: test/comment.test.ts::a missing PR URL falls back to the repository gh resolved
findings.reason: The unsupported gh pr view --json baseRepository fallback is replaced with gh repo view.

findings.claim: Concurrent streaming finders share a dedupe set, so the cached representative and report order depend on finder completion timing.
findings.test: test/engine.test.ts::v2.1.162 dedupes in finder order even when a later finder finishes first
findings.reason: Streaming dedup flushes in finder order and verified findings are sorted before the sweep/synthesis.

findings.claim: When the text synthesizer over-emits and the normalizer truncates the report, the engine records `truncatedFrom = emitted.length + 1` instead of the known survivor count, so the renderer claims the report was cut from a number that is far too low.
findings.test: test/engine.test.ts::a truncated text-synthesis report uses the verified survivor count
findings.reason: A truncated synthesis report reports the verified survivor count as the pre-cap lower bound.

findings.claim: The generated git allow-rules require the full `-c` hardening prefix, while the spawned agents' contracts tell them to run only `git diff/log/show/blame` plus `--no-ext-diff/--no-textconv`, so the commands the children actually construct are denied.
findings.test: test/prompts.test.ts::the three review agents share one read-only policy module
findings.reason: The agent contract now tells children to prefix git commands with the same -c hardening the permission table requires.

findings.claim: The shared read-only policy is installed by awaiting `ctx.agent.transform` during setup with no error handling, so one rejecting agent update aborts the whole plugin registration instead of falling back to the Markdown permissions.
findings.test: test/agent-policy.test.ts::installReviewAgentPolicy replaces each review agent's permissions
findings.reason: A rejected agent.transform no longer aborts plugin registration; the Markdown fallback remains.

findings.claim: The abort listener dispatches `interrupt?.(...)?.catch(...)`, which does not catch a synchronous throw, so an interrupt failure escapes the AbortSignal listener.
findings.test: test/runner.test.ts::a synchronous interrupt failure does not escape cancellation
findings.reason: A synchronous session.interrupt throw is caught inside the abort listener.

findings.claim: `session.remove` is awaited inside `finally` with only `.catch` on the returned promise, so a synchronous throw there replaces the child's already-captured result.
findings.test: test/runner.test.ts::a synchronous session.remove failure keeps the captured result
findings.reason: session.remove sync throws are caught and a never-settling remove is bounded.

findings.claim: PR patch and head metadata are fetched in parallel, so a push during discovery can pair stale line anchors with the new head when `--comment` posts.
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts::a PR review downloads the patch once and verifies the head
findings.reason: The PR patch is captured between two matching head reads; an unverified pair refuses inline comments.

findings.claim: The `--comment` posting call is awaited outside the review's try/catch, so a rejected gh/exec call turns a completed review into a command failure and discards the report.
findings.test: test/comment.test.ts
findings.reason: Comment posting is inside the review error boundary, so a failed gh/exec call still returns the report.

findings.claim: A failed PR `gh pr view` metadata call pushes a comment-only warning into `scope.warnings`, which the plugin turns into `result.partial`, so a PR review whose diff and file list were fully recovered is reported as an incomplete review.
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts::a failed PR metadata call still uses the cached patch
findings.reason: A missing PR head is a comment-only concern and no longer marks the review partial.

findings.claim: The host gate refuses `--comment` for a PR-number review whenever the local `origin` remote is absent or not GitHub, even though the PR's own GitHub URL was already captured in `scope.prUrl`.
findings.test: test/comment.test.ts::a PR-number review posts when the local origin is not GitHub
findings.reason: A captured PR URL is authoritative for the comment host even when the local origin is absent or a mirror.

findings.claim: A contiguous 1-based grouped-verdict list shorter than the group is discarded entirely instead of being shifted, so a verifier that covers only part of the group loses every verdict, including CONFIRMED ones.
findings.test: test/json.test.ts::asGroupVerdicts shifts 1-based lists, including partial ones, but not after index 0 was dropped
findings.reason: A partial contiguous 1-based verdict list is shifted instead of being discarded.

findings.claim: Sweep gaps are pushed into `kept`/`surviving` and then counted by the deterministic summary (and the synthesizer prompt) as findings that "survived verification", even though sweep candidates are explicitly never verified and are marked PLAUSIBLE with no evidence.
findings.test: test/engine.test.ts::a sweep gap is not presented as independently verified
findings.reason: Sweep gaps are labeled as gap-sweep findings, not as findings that survived verification.

findings.claim: The gh-api failure branch formats the anchor itself instead of reusing renderedLocation, which the same loop already uses for its other two failure messages.
findings.test: test/comment.test.ts
findings.reason: gh-api failure messages use renderedLocation like the sibling failure branches.

findings.claim: The full-diff capture promises are started before the file listings are validated and are never awaited when every listing fails, so a failed discovery leaves full `git diff` children running and buffering output nobody reads.
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts::a failed file listing does not start full diff captures
findings.reason: Diff captures start only after the file listings are validated, so a failed discovery does not leave full diff children running.

findings.claim: For a --comment/--post run the review root is resolved with `resolveReviewRoot` (which calls `classifyTarget`) and then `resolveScope` classifies the same target a second time, repeating every git probe.
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts
findings.reason: Host detection passes its target classification into resolveScope instead of classifying twice.

findings.claim: `--post` without `--comment` triggers `detectHostDetails`, including the `gh auth status --hostname` network probe, although the only consumer of the result (`postNotice`) branches solely on GitLab.
findings.test: test/comment.test.ts::detectHostDetails can skip the enterprise auth probe
findings.reason: --post without --comment skips the gh auth network probe.

findings.claim: `trackActivity` keeps a process-wide subscription to high-frequency stream event types and mutates a shared map for every delta of every session, review or not, for the plugin's whole lifetime.
findings.test: test/runner.test.ts::trackActivity ignores sessions outside the review child set
findings.reason: Activity tracking filters to review child sessions, so unrelated traffic cannot evict a live reading.

findings.claim: The third conjunct of `willSynthesize` is entailed by the first (`surviving.length > 1`) and can never be false.
findings.test: test/engine.test.ts
findings.reason: The entailed willSynthesize conjunct is removed.

findings.claim: `unmergedFallback` duplicates `deterministicReport`'s dedupe/cap/truncation accounting with only a different summary.
findings.test: test/engine.test.ts
findings.reason: unmergedFallback reuses deterministicReport's dedupe/cap/truncation accounting.

findings.claim: The progress and max-findings notices hand-roll singular/plural forms (`candidate(s)`, `changed file(s)`, `=== 1 ?`) instead of calling the shared pluralize/pluralWord helpers.
findings.test: test/engine.test.ts
findings.reason: Progress and limit notices use the shared pluralize/pluralWord helpers.

findings.claim: `token.toLowerCase() === "ultra"` is redundant because `isLevelToken` already accepts `ultra`.
findings.test: test/parse.test.ts
findings.reason: The redundant ultra spelling check is removed; isLevelToken owns the rule.

findings.claim: buildFinders hardcodes angle-A..E and slices the joined corpus by position, while prompts.ts owns the angle fragments and already exports labeled lens lists for cleanup.
findings.test: test/engine.test.ts
findings.reason: buildFinders zips the exported labeled correctness lenses instead of slicing joined prompt text by position.

findings.claim: ROLE_TOOLS/REVIEW_AGENT_IDS hardcodes the same review agent IDs that engine.ts declares in AGENT_IDS, with no shared source.
findings.test: test/agent-policy.test.ts
findings.reason: Agent IDs come from one shared agent-ids module used by the engine and the policy installer.

findings.claim: Policy installation is made idempotent by searching for a hardcoded hardening substring instead of replacing the permission list.
findings.test: test/agent-policy.test.ts::installReviewAgentPolicy replaces each review agent's permissions
findings.reason: Policy installation assigns the full permission list, which is idempotent and drops stale rules.

findings.claim: `willApplyFix` re-implements `fixAction`'s predicate and duplicates the later `applyFix` value.
findings.test: test/engine.test.ts
findings.reason: hasReportFindings reuses fixAction's applyFix result instead of duplicating its predicate.

findings.claim: OUTCOMES/isOutcome is a second hand-maintained copy of the outcome enum declared in REPORT_FINDINGS_SCHEMA, which reportFindingError otherwise walks programmatically.
findings.test: test/reportfindings.test.ts
findings.reason: The accepted outcome list is derived from REPORT_FINDINGS_SCHEMA and validated once.

findings.claim: Every child prompt embeds a valid result as the `Expected shape` example, so the parser has to hand-detect schema echoes at five call sites instead of making the example un-echoable.
findings.test: test/json.test.ts::every generated schema example is detected as an echo
findings.reason: Generated schema examples carry a sentinel, so a new result kind is detected without another hand-written branch.

findings.claim: startsWithText repeats the text-part extraction logic of messageText instead of sharing one transcript-part walker.
findings.test: test/runner.test.ts
findings.reason: messageText and startsWithText share one text-part walker.

findings.claim: Every exec in `resolveScope` repeats the same two-line aborted/timedOut guard instead of one shared helper.
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts
findings.reason: Scope discovery uses one assertExec failure policy instead of repeated aborted/timedOut guards.

findings.claim: `filesFromDiff` is exported but has no caller; the PR file-list recovery its comment documents is implemented by `scanPatchChurn` and `gh pr diff --name-only`, leaving a second patch parser that is never exercised.
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts
findings.reason: filesFromDiff is a thin view over the one patch walker instead of a second parser.

pastReviewItems.reason: Host detection classifies once and passes the result into resolveScope.

pastReviewItems.claim: A commented PR re-fetches URL/head with two gh pr view calls
pastReviewItems.reason: PR-number reviews use the URL/head captured with the patch; branch reviews fetch number, head, and base in one call. A missing field still needs a fallback read, which is not a correctness defect.

pastReviewItems.claim: Displayed diff command omits the orchestrator's -c hardening flags
pastReviewItems.test: test/prompts.test.ts::the three review agents share one read-only policy module
pastReviewItems.reason: The displayed command carries the -c flags; the agent contract tells children to use them, and the fallback policy allows that command.

pastReviewItems.claim: Permission table duplicated across three agent files
pastReviewItems.test: test/prompts.test.ts::the three review agents share one read-only policy module
pastReviewItems.reason: The full table is installed from agent-policy.ts. The Markdown fallback is now generated from the same module by scripts/sync-agent-policy.ts, so it is no longer a hand-copied table; a test fails when it drifts.
pastReviewItems.note: Superseded by DELTA2-16: the fallback block is generated, not hand-copied.

pastReviewItems.reason: For scopeKind=branch it is the user's diff base; otherwise it is the checked-out head. resolvePrInfo already re-reads the current branch for the branch kind. A headBranch field would be a larger scope-model change with no observed wrong output.

pastReviewItems.claim: if (scope.diffBase) is unreachable after the earlier guard
pastReviewItems.reason: The dead branch is removed; the base checks run unconditionally for a branch-shaped review.
The get-failure and backoff blocks are shared helpers.
gitlabComment is absent from the plugin; only the recovered-corpus research notes still mention it. The live path refuses GitLab comments.
The prompts differ in angle count, cap, intro, and verifier fragment, and must stay byte-exact to the recovered corpus.

deltaRuns.note: The report was truncated and partial, so the visible 15 were fixed; the next pass runs with --max-findings all to classify the tail.

findings.claim: Every generated example now carries `__example: true`, so a model that fills in the example template but keeps that key has its real answer rejected as an echo.
findings.test: test/json.test.ts::a filled-in example that kept the sentinel is a real result
findings.reason: Only partially filled examples are echoes; a filled-in answer that kept the sentinel is accepted.

findings.claim: Removing the contiguity check from the 1-based plan test lets one off-by-one index flip an entire zero-based plan to 1-based.
findings.test: test/engine.test.ts::an out-of-range index does not flip a zero-based plan to 1-based
findings.reason: A 1-based plan must be a contiguous run starting at 1; one out-of-range index no longer flips the plan.

findings.claim: asGroupVerdicts shifts any list starting at 1, including non-contiguous zero-based subsets
findings.test: test/json.test.ts::asGroupVerdicts shifts full 1-based lists and refuses ambiguous partial lists
findings.reason: Only a full 1-based group-verdict list is shifted; ambiguous partial lists are refused rather than mispaired.

findings.claim: When the text synthesizer report is truncated, truncatedFrom is set to the pre-merge survivor count, so the notice reports unverified sweep gaps and merged-away entries as 'verified findings'.
findings.test: test/engine.test.ts::a truncated text-synthesis report uses the verified survivor count
findings.reason: The truncation notice counts verified findings, excluding sweep gaps.

findings.claim: The prompt's diff command now drops the pathspec for any control character, including tabs and CRs that the child permission table does not deny.
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts::a tab in a path stays in the runnable command
findings.reason: Tabs are not denied by the child policy and no longer omit the pathspec; control characters renderPath rewrites still do.

findings.claim: The partial-capture numstat fallback now asks only the failed plan entries and then assigns their subtotal to diffLines, discarding the line count already computed from the successful captures' patch.
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts::a partial capture adds failed numstat to the successful patch total
findings.reason: Failed capture numstat is added to the successful patch total instead of replacing it.

findings.claim: Pinning the reviewed PR head now requires the trailing metadata read to succeed, so a transient gh failure disables inline comments even when the patch and first metadata agree.
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts::an unavailable head check leaves the PR head unverified; test/comment.test.ts::a PR-number review without a verified head posts a general comment
findings.reason: Superseded by DELTA2-05: an unavailable head check no longer pins the head; the findings are posted as a general comment.

findings.claim: Passing includeConventions=false for 162 cells skips discoverConventions entirely, so scope.claudeMdFiles is empty even though renderScope prints that path list to every finder and verifier and the no-conventions text tells them to read those files.
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts::includeConventions false lists paths but skips the CLAUDE.md text
findings.reason: Convention paths are discovered even when the text is skipped for a 162 cell.

findings.claim: Replacing the base-repository lookup with `gh repo view` reintroduces the fork-clone hazard the old refusal guarded against.
findings.test: test/comment.test.ts::a branch review with no PR URL refuses instead of guessing the repository
findings.reason: The gh repo view fallback is limited to PR-number reviews; branch reviews refuse when the URL is missing.

findings.claim: Summary-comment fallback reposts the same findings when a retried inline post fails transiently
findings.test: test/comment.test.ts::an existing general comment is not reposted
findings.reason: The general comment carries a stable hidden marker, so a retry does not post a duplicate.

findings.claim: In the streaming path, verification of a finder's candidates cannot start until every earlier finder has returned, so child latency is added to the critical path.
findings.test: test/engine.test.ts::v2.1.162 verifies a later finder before an earlier slow finder returns
findings.reason: Each finder verifies immediately; cross-finder dedup happens after all finders return in finder order.

findings.claim: PR discovery now makes three serial gh network calls and re-parses the full metadata JSON (with the file list) several times per review.
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts::a local PR review skips the post-capture head check
findings.reason: The post-capture check is a head-only read and is skipped when --comment will not post.

findings.claim: The 58-line fallback permission table re-implements agent-policy.ts's SHELL_DENY/READ_ONLY_POLICY rules in three Markdown files and is already out of sync.
findings.test: test/prompts.test.ts::the Markdown fallback carries every shared shell deny rule
findings.reason: The fallback deny list is synced with READ_ONLY_POLICY and tested against it.

findings.claim: `ctx.session.remove` is detached from its receiver before being called
findings.test: test/runner.test.ts::session.remove keeps its receiver
findings.reason: session.remove is called as a method, preserving its receiver.

findings.claim: Child teardown awaits a 5s `session.remove` timeout inside `runInChild`'s finally, blocking the concurrency slot that could start the next child.
findings.test: test/runner.test.ts::a hanging session.remove is bounded
findings.reason: Child removal is fire-and-forget with an unref'd timeout; it no longer blocks the concurrency slot.

deltaRuns.note: The report was complete (19 findings, below the 32 cap). Eighteen were fixed in 54fafeb; DELTA2-10 was reclassified in DELTA3-15 (pluralWord dropped the count) and fixed in f5d68ed.

findings.claim: Cross-finder dedupe after verification keeps the lowest finder index, so a REFUTED duplicate discards a CONFIRMED copy of the same claim.
findings.test: test/engine.test.ts::streaming dedupe keeps a confirmed duplicate over a refuted one
findings.reason: Cross-finder dedupe keeps the strongest verdict; a refuted duplicate no longer discards a confirmed copy.

findings.claim: The new placeholder-count echo check no longer recognizes a single-verdict schema echo once the tool boundary strips `__example`.
findings.test: test/json.test.ts::a stripped single-verdict echo is still detected
findings.reason: A top-level verdict with the placeholder evidence is an echo even after the tool boundary strips `__example`.

findings.claim: `countSamplePlaceholders` counts each occurrence of a placeholder string, so any payload that names a sample path twice reaches the `>= 2` echo threshold even when every other field is a genuine result. [same root cause also at: .opencode/plugins/code-review-opencode/schemas.ts:166]
findings.test: test/json.test.ts::repeated real paths in a candidates payload are not an echo
findings.reason: Echo detection counts distinct placeholders and requires two of the three finding placeholders, so repeated real sample paths are not an echo.

findings.claim: The general-comment retry marker hashes only the current failed subset, so a retry whose failure set changes posts a second general comment that duplicates findings. [same root cause also at: .opencode/plugins/code-review-opencode/comment.ts:565]
findings.test: test/comment.test.ts::the general comment marker stays stable when the failed subset changes
findings.reason: The marker hashes the full result, not the current unposted subset, so a retry with a different inline success set does not repost.

findings.claim: `prHeadVerified` fails open when the trailing head read is unavailable, so comments can be pinned to a head whose patch was never captured.
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts::an unavailable head check leaves the PR head unverified; test/comment.test.ts::a PR-number review without a verified head posts a general comment
findings.reason: Head-only reads bracket the patch; an unavailable check leaves the head unverified and posting falls back to a head-independent general comment. Supersedes DELTA1-07.

findings.claim: A partial 1-based group-verdict list is no longer refused or shifted, so its verdicts are attached to neighbouring candidates.
findings.test: test/json.test.ts::asGroupVerdicts shifts full 1-based lists and refuses ambiguous partial lists
findings.reason: A partial list without index 0 is refused instead of being attached to neighbouring candidates.

findings.claim: `labelFor` omits only the pathspec when it contains shell metacharacters; the repository root is still emitted as `git -C '<root>'`, so a root containing `&` or `;` produces a command that the agents' own deny rules reject. [same root cause also at: .opencode/plugins/code-review-opencode/scope.ts:410]
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts::a repository root with a shell metacharacter uses a relative -C path
findings.reason: A metacharacter root is replaced by a realpath-relative -C path; if that is also unsafe, the runnable command is omitted.

findings.claim: `applyIndexPlan` no longer treats a contiguous 1-based subset as 1-based, so a synthesizer's 1-based decision subset is applied to the wrong survivors.
findings.test: test/engine.test.ts::a contiguous subset with no index 0 falls back instead of guessing
findings.reason: Superseded by DELTA4-16: an ambiguous contiguous subset now falls back to the deterministic report instead of guessing a base.

findings.claim: `installReviewAgentPolicy` replaces the full permission list, dropping host/user permission rules that had been merged onto the review agents.
findings.test: test/agent-policy.test.ts::installReviewAgentPolicy replaces governed rules and keeps host extensions
findings.reason: The policy is merged with existing rules; ungoverned host actions are preserved and governed actions are rebuilt from the policy.

findings.claim: The finder progress line drops the candidate count, so the progress message no longer reports how many candidates have been found.
findings.test: test/finding.test.ts::pluralize includes the count while pluralWord does not
findings.reason: The finder progress line now uses `pluralize(event.candidates, "candidate")`, which includes the number. The earlier `pluralWord` call rendered only the noun.

findings.claim: unmergedFallback overwrites the sweep-aware deterministicReport summary, so a failed synthesis still advertises unverified sweep gaps as verified findings. [same root cause also at: .opencode/plugins/code-review-opencode/engine.ts:521, .opencode/plugins/code-review-opencode/prompts.ts:952]
findings.test: test/engine.test.ts::a failed synthesis keeps the sweep-aware deterministic summary
findings.reason: Fallback notes are appended to the deterministic summary, which distinguishes sweep gaps from verified findings.

findings.claim: The deterministic-report result is applied by hand in three places, and only `unmergedFallback` updates the duplicate accounting.
findings.test: test/engine.test.ts::a failed synthesis keeps the sweep-aware deterministic summary
findings.reason: All deterministic fallbacks go through applyDeterministic, which updates dedupe, cap, truncation, and duplicate accounting together.

findings.claim: PR scope discovery now awaits the metadata download before starting the patch download, and adds a third serial head read, where the patch and metadata used to run concurrently.
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts::a PR review downloads the patch once and verifies the head
findings.reason: Metadata and patch downloads run concurrently; two cheap head-only reads bracket the patch.

findings.claim: The plan diff captures now start only after all name-status listings complete, removing the previous overlap between the listing probes and the `git diff` patch capture.
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts::a failed file listing awaits the already-started diff captures
findings.reason: Captures start with the listings; the all-listings-failed path awaits them before throwing.

findings.claim: The new `sleep` helper duplicates the identical inline delay still used at runner.ts:723 inside the same poll loop.
findings.test: test/runner.test.ts (poll and backoff suites)
findings.reason: The main poll now uses the same sleep helper as the backoff and get-failure branches.

findings.claim: The newly added 60-line fallback shell permission table hand-copies agent-policy.ts's READ_ONLY_POLICY/SHELL_DENY rules into three Markdown agents instead of deriving from the one policy source.
findings.test: test/agent-policy.test.ts::the Markdown fallback permissions are generated from the shared policy
findings.reason: The Markdown permissions block is generated by renderAgentPolicyYaml and scripts/sync-agent-policy.ts; a test fails when it drifts.

findings.claim: The new module-level `compareFindings` re-implements the file/line/summary/failure_scenario ordering that is still written inline for `ranked` at engine.ts:1187-1197 instead of being called there.
findings.test: test/engine.test.ts (deterministic ordering suite)
findings.reason: The ranked sort now calls compareFindings instead of an inline copy.

findings.claim: The new branch/ref normalization re-implements the exported `samePrBase` policy from comment.ts:302-313 (strip refs/heads and refs/remotes, then match a prefix only when it is a real remote name) instead of sharing it.
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts (branch/remote-target suite); test/comment.test.ts (samePrBase suite)
findings.reason: Ref normalization and remote-prefix matching live in refs.ts and are shared by scope and posting.

findings.claim: `filesFromDiff` has no callers, so the diff rewrote an untested wrapper instead of deleting it.
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts (patch walker suite)
findings.reason: The unused filesFromDiff wrapper was deleted; tests call scanPatchChurn directly.

findings.claim: The preserved filter drops only the exact `{action:"*", resource:"*"}` rule, so any other existing rule whose action is `*` survives the merge — unlike the previous install, which dropped every `*`-action rule before appending the policy.
findings.test: test/agent-policy.test.ts::installReviewAgentPolicy replaces governed rules and keeps host extensions
findings.reason: The merge now drops every existing broad `*` action rule, so a host rule such as `*:/tmp/* allow` cannot sit after the deny-all.

findings.claim: Creating the dedupe `seen` set per finder instead of sharing it spends each finder's hard verifier quota re-verifying another finder's duplicate, so unique candidates are dropped as budget-exhausted.
findings.test: test/engine.test.ts::a confirmed duplicate does not consume another finder's verifier slots; test/engine.test.ts::v2.1.162 dedupes in finder order even when a later finder finishes first
findings.reason: A per-claim representative is skipped without spending a slot when its verdict is kept; a refuted representative still gets one duplicate retry, and the lowest finder index owns the reported text.

findings.claim: Removing the `allowSubsetBase`/full-plan guard from `applyIndexPlan` changes the pre-verification caller `applyCandidateDedup`, which never passed that flag: a zero-based dedup plan that only names contiguous indices 1..k is now shifted as 1-based.
findings.test: test/engine.test.ts::a contiguous dedup subset stays zero-based
findings.reason: The candidate-dedup caller requires a full 1-based plan; a zero-based subset that starts at 1 is no longer shifted.

findings.claim: Changing the echo check from `every` to `some` lets one example-looking item reject an entire genuine candidates/verdicts payload.
findings.test: test/json.test.ts::one partly filled template item does not reject the real candidates
findings.reason: A partly filled template item is dropped from the payload instead of rejecting the whole candidates list.

findings.claim: `schemas.ts` now stamps `__example: true` into every child example, and `isSchemaEcho` treats that sentinel plus a single sample placeholder value as an echo, so a filled-in payload that kept the sentinel is discarded when any field matches a sample string.
findings.test: test/json.test.ts::a real sample path with the sentinel is not an echo
findings.reason: The sentinel fallback ignores the file-path placeholder, so a real file named `path/to/file.ts` does not discard a filled-in answer.

findings.claim: The missing-PR-URL fallback resolves the repository with `gh repo view` in the cwd, which names the fork in a fork clone instead of the PR's base repository.
findings.test: test/comment.test.ts::a PR-number review with no PR URL refuses instead of using the fork; test/comment.test.ts::a missing PR URL refuses instead of using the repository gh resolved
findings.reason: A missing PR URL refuses for both branch and PR-number reviews; `gh repo view` can name a fork with its own PR of the same number.

findings.claim: The retry marker hashes the full finding set but is matched against a general comment that only contains the previously unposted subset, so a later run can report findings as posted when they are not.
findings.test: test/comment.test.ts::a finding missing from the existing general comment is posted
findings.reason: The general comment carries one marker per finding, so a changed failure subset neither hides an unposted finding nor reposts one that is present.

findings.claim: The HEAD that the new bracket reads prove is never used to set prHeadOid, so when the metadata read fails the code marks the pair verified but leaves prHeadOid unset and --comment treats a verified patch as unverified.
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts::a verified head is pinned when only the metadata read fails
findings.reason: The verified bracket head is stored separately and used for prHeadOid even when the metadata payload is unavailable.

findings.claim: The retry marker hashes the rendered, order-dependent full findings body, so the same finding set reported in a different order produces a new marker and a duplicate general PR comment.
findings.test: test/comment.test.ts::the general comment marker stays stable when the failed subset changes; test/comment.test.ts::a finding missing from the existing general comment is posted
findings.reason: Per-finding markers are order-independent and subset-independent, so the same finding set in a different order produces the same markers.

findings.claim: The retry guard suppresses the summary comment only when the paginated `gh api` comment-list call succeeds and contains the marker; when that call fails, control falls through to the posting branch even though a previous run may already have posted the identical comment.
findings.test: test/comment.test.ts::a failed existing-comment check does not post a duplicate
findings.reason: An unavailable existing-comment check now fails closed instead of posting a comment that may duplicate a previous run.

findings.claim: `labelFor` omits an unsafe pathspec and relativizes an unsafe root, but it still renders `spec.range` — which comes verbatim from the user's branch/range target — so a legal branch name containing `&`, `;`, `$`, or a backtick produces a displayed diff command that the same permission table denies.
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts::a branch target with a shell metacharacter omits the runnable command
findings.reason: An unsafe range omits the whole runnable command; the embedded diff is still scoped.

findings.claim: truncatedFrom is raised to ranked.length - sweepGaps, counting findings the synthesizer merged away as if the report cap cut them.
findings.test: test/engine.test.ts::a truncated text-synthesis report reports the proven lower bound
findings.reason: The pre-cap count is the emitted length plus one, not the survivor count; merged-away findings are not reported as cap-cut.

findings.claim: `deterministicReport`/`applyDecisions` report `truncatedFrom` as the total ranked length, which includes unverified sweep gaps, while `formatReportFindings` and `formatHuman` label that count as verified findings.
findings.test: test/format.test.ts::the truncation notice calls the pre-cap count findings, not verified findings
findings.reason: The renderer calls the pre-cap count findings, since it can include sweep gaps that were never independently verified.

findings.claim: The new sweep-gap intro interpolates `pluralWord(gaps, "sweep gap")`, which returns only the noun, so the synthesizer headline reads "N findings (M verified, sweep gaps)" without the number of unverified gaps. [same root cause also at: .opencode/plugins/code-review-opencode/prompts.ts:952]
findings.test: test/prompts.test.ts::the sweep-gap intro includes the gap count
findings.reason: The synth prompts render the gap count before the plural noun.

findings.claim: The finder progress event is rendered with `pluralWord(event.candidates, "candidate")`, which yields only "candidate"/"candidates"; the numeric count printed by the previous `${event.candidates} candidate(s)` form is dropped.
findings.test: test/finding.test.ts::pluralize includes the count while pluralWord does not
findings.reason: The finder progress line uses `pluralize`, which includes the number. This corrects DELTA2-10: the previous `pluralWord` call rendered only the noun.

findings.claim: The new guard refuses any non-empty verdict list that lacks index 0, including a legitimate zero-based list with gaps, so valid verdicts for candidates 1 and 3 are now discarded.
findings.test: test/json.test.ts::asGroupVerdicts shifts full 1-based lists and refuses ambiguous partial lists
findings.reason: Only a contiguous partial run starting at 1 is refused; a non-contiguous zero-based list with gaps is kept.

findings.claim: `dedupeVerified` rebuilds `verified` from one representative per `dedupKey162` bucket, so a REFUTED copy that collides with a CONFIRMED copy disappears from `refuted` as well, removing it from the sweep's known/refuted guard.
findings.test: test/engine.test.ts::a skipped duplicate stays in the sweep guard when a confirmed copy wins
findings.reason: Skipped and deduped duplicates are added to the sweep's known list and exact-claim set, so the sweep cannot resurrect them as fresh gaps.

findings.claim: Dropping the `!isPathTarget` guard from the branch-recording condition makes a path-target review record `scope.branch`, so `--comment` now treats a path-filtered diff as the current branch's PR diff.
findings.reason: Invalid: a path-filtered diff is a subset of the same base/head PR diff; the included file's line numbers are unchanged, postComments verifies the local HEAD, base, and merge-base, and diffSideMap only anchors the reviewed path. The delta-1 change deliberately enabled path reviews to post.

findings.claim: `assertExec(fullRef, ...)` turns the new `rev-parse --symbolic-full-name` refinement into a hard failure of the whole review, even though it only decides whether the target names the checked-out branch.
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts::a failed symbolic-full-name probe does not fail a branch review
findings.reason: The symbolic-full-name probe is optional; a failed probe falls back to the abbreviated-name comparison.

findings.claim: In the new `complete` branch of `readCapped`, a character budget smaller than the truncation marker truncates the text with no `…(truncated)` marker. [same root cause also at: .opencode/plugins/code-review-opencode/scope.ts:953]
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts::a conventions budget smaller than the marker still marks truncation
findings.reason: A budget too small for content and marker returns the marker instead of a silent fragment.

findings.claim: The trailing head read, and its unconditional one-retry loop, run after the patch/metadata fetches even when `gh pr diff` already failed, adding up to two more gh invocations and their full timeout before the error is raised.
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts::a failed patch fetch does not run the trailing head read
findings.reason: The patch/metadata pair is checked before the trailing head read, so a failed patch does not spend two more gh timeouts.

findings.claim: `OUTCOMES` is now read from `FINDING_SCHEMA.properties.outcome.enum` at module load, but the schema is typed loosely enough that removing or renaming `outcome` yields `undefined` and crashes validation at runtime instead of failing the build.
findings.test: test/reportfindings.test.ts::the adapter schema mirrors the recovered tool schema
findings.reason: The outcome enum is read with a fallback empty array, so a schema edit cannot crash validation; a test asserts the enum is present.

findings.claim: The new unverified-head fallback still resolves the live PR head with an extra `gh pr view --json headRefOid` call although the value is not required or used on that path.
findings.test: test/comment.test.ts::a PR-number review without a verified head posts a general comment
findings.reason: The unverified-head path skips the unused head probe.

findings.claim: `postComments` builds the whole-patch `diffSideMap` even when `headUnverified` forces every finding into the general-comment path and the map is never queried.
findings.test: test/comment.test.ts::a PR-number review without a verified head posts a general comment
findings.reason: The diff side map is built lazily inside the inline branch; the general-comment path skips the patch parse.

findings.claim: The general-comment idempotency guard pages through every issue comment on the PR and downloads all bodies before posting, on every invocation that has unposted findings.
findings.reason: Accepted: the paginated scan is the only reliable way to find a per-finding marker in an arbitrary earlier comment; a last-page-only check could miss it and post a duplicate. It runs only when findings fail inline. A persistent marker cache would be a larger design change and can go stale across processes.

findings.claim: The explicit-path validation now also runs before the engine path, where `resolveScope` immediately repeats the same `findGitRoot`/`realpathSync` walk (and host detection has usually run `resolveTargetPath` once more).
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts (path-target suite)
findings.reason: The explicit-path pre-check now runs only on the inline and single-pass prompt paths; the engine path lets resolveScope perform the check once.

findings.claim: `SHELL_DENIED` is a second hand-maintained copy of the shell deny rules: it mirrors the control-operator patterns but omits the substring denies (`difftool`, `--output`, `--paginate`, `--config-env`, ` -O`, ...) that `labelFor` must also avoid.
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts::a path containing a denied substring omits the pathspec
findings.reason: The deny globs and the substrings used by labelFor come from one shell-policy module, so a denied substring is omitted from the runnable command.

findings.claim: The full ~125-line read-only shell policy is copy-pasted into all three agent Markdown files (differing only in the tool allow), and the only mechanism keeping them equal to `agent-policy.ts` is a manual `scripts/sync-agent-policy.ts` run with no check mode or CI/test invocation.
findings.test: test/agent-policy.test.ts::the agent-policy sync check passes; test/agent-policy.test.ts::the Markdown fallback permissions are generated from the shared policy
findings.reason: The sync script has a `--check` mode and a test runs it; the generated block is also compared directly to renderAgentPolicyYaml.

findings.claim: Each finder's verified results are sorted with `compareFindings` here and then the whole array is sorted again at engine.ts:1083, while `mapLimit` already preserves input order, so the per-finder sort is redundant.
findings.test: test/engine.test.ts (streaming determinism suite)
findings.reason: The redundant per-finder sort was removed; the global compareFindings sort remains the single ordering step.

findings.claim: The `git diff --quiet` exit>1 failure block is copy-pasted at scope.ts:1504, 1557, and 1617 instead of being added to the new `assertExec` helper that the diff introduced as the one failure policy.
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts (worktree probe suites)
findings.reason: The three `git diff --quiet` failure blocks now share assertQuietProbe.

findings.claim: The branch-name check hand-writes the normalized equality that the imported sameRefName helper already implements.
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts::a remote-prefixed current branch includes uncommitted changes; test/comment.test.ts (samePrBase suite)
findings.reason: The branch-name comparisons use the shared sameRefName helper instead of hand-written normalized equality.

deltaRuns.note: The report was complete (31 findings, below the 32 cap). Thirty were fixed in 0b217cd (DELTA4-29 in f5d68ed); DELTA4-15 is accepted as the same full-marker-scan trade-off recorded in DELTA3-25.

findings.claim: The `__example` sentinel check rejects a whole text payload when any item still carries a template placeholder, even when other items are real findings, contradicting the new per-item placeholder drop.
findings.test: test/json.test.ts::a sentinel payload with real items is not an echo
findings.reason: A sentinel payload with at least one real list item is kept; the normalizer drops the placeholder item.

findings.claim: `zeroDropped` is computed from the raw verdict list before placeholder verdicts are dropped, so a copied index-0 template verdict disables the 1-based shift for the real 1..n verdicts.
findings.test: test/json.test.ts::a placeholder verdict at index 0 does not disable a 1-based shift
findings.reason: A placeholder index 0 is ignored when deciding zeroDropped, so the real 1..n verdicts still shift.

findings.claim: When a lower-index finder reuses a representative's verdict, the report re-emits that finder's own unverified failure scenario and line while carrying a CONFIRMED verdict the verifier earned on the other finder's text. [same root cause also at: .opencode/plugins/code-review-opencode/engine.ts:1070]
findings.test: test/engine.test.ts::a lower-index recheck never presents unverified text as confirmed
findings.reason: A later-arriving lower-index copy is verified before its text can replace the representative, so the report never carries an unverified scenario under a confirmed verdict.

findings.claim: `findingMarker` hashes model-generated summary and failure_scenario text, so a re-run whose synthesizer or deterministic fallback rewords the same finding produces a new marker and the existing general-comment scan misses it.
findings.test: test/comment.test.ts::the finding marker is stable across the also-at suffix and punctuation
findings.reason: The marker hashes the normalized base claim, so an also-at suffix or punctuation change does not repost the finding.

findings.claim: `dedupeVerified` records a dropped refuted copy in `refutedDropped` only when the surviving copy has a defined verdict, so two refuted copies of one 5-line bucket leave the survivor's scenario as the only refuted evidence.
findings.test: test/engine.test.ts::distinct refuted scenarios both stay in the refuted guard
findings.reason: Distinct refuted scenarios are both kept for the sweep; only an exact duplicate of the representative's scenario is skipped.

findings.claim: Refuted duplicates dropped from the report are appended to the user-visible `refuted` array, so a claim confirmed by one verifier and refuted by another is reported as both a finding and a refutation.
findings.test: test/engine.test.ts::a lower-index recheck never presents unverified text as confirmed
findings.reason: A refuted duplicate of a kept claim is a duplicate, not a refutation; the user-visible refuted list excludes it.

findings.claim: `normalizeCandidatesCall` silently drops placeholder-shaped items without a note, so a payload containing only the prompt's template is rejected with a misleading 'needs file, summary, and failure_scenario' error even though those fields are present. [same root cause also at: .opencode/plugins/code-review-opencode/json.ts:884]
findings.test: test/json.test.ts::a placeholder-only payload names the schema example
findings.reason: A payload that contains only the schema example gets a specific error instead of the misleading missing-fields message.

findings.claim: readCapped returns the fixed 13-character "\n…(truncated)" marker when budget <= marker.length, exceeding the caller's cap instead of respecting it. [same root cause also at: .opencode/plugins/code-review-opencode/scope.ts:980]
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts::readCapped keeps a tiny budget while still signalling truncation
findings.reason: A tiny budget returns the short ellipsis marker and never exceeds the caller's cap.

findings.claim: `mergeReviewAgentPermissions` keeps host rules for ungoverned actions after the catch-all deny, so a host/user allow for a write-capable action is no longer neutralised by the read-only policy.
findings.test: test/agent-policy.test.ts::installReviewAgentPolicy replaces governed rules and keeps host extensions
findings.reason: Only webfetch/websearch host extensions are preserved; edit/write/patch allows are dropped so a review child cannot modify the tree.

findings.claim: A failed inline `gh api` call is treated as 'not posted' and the same finding is then added to the general comment, but a timeout or 5xx does not prove the review comment was not created.
findings.test: test/comment.test.ts::an ambiguous inline timeout is not repeated in a general comment
findings.reason: A timeout or 5xx inline post is ambiguous and is not repeated in the general comment; the failure is reported for a retry.

findings.claim: `hardLimitApplies(usesEngine, hasReportFindings)` is equivalent to `usesEngine || kind === "reportfindings"`, so the new `(!usesEngine || applyFix)` refinement and the one-line exported helper are dead structure. [same root cause also at: .opencode/plugins/code-review-opencode/parse.ts:502]
findings.test: test/parse.test.ts (max-findings suite)
findings.reason: The dead hardLimitApplies helper was removed; the call site uses usesEngine || kind === reportfindings directly.

findings.claim: `labelFor` omits a pathspec that trips a deny substring and still renders the full diff command, so the advertised command can review files outside the requested path target. [same root cause also at: .opencode/plugins/code-review-opencode/scope.ts:462]
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts::a path with a shell metacharacter omits the runnable command; test/scope.test.ts::a path containing a denied substring omits the runnable command
findings.reason: An unsafe pathspec omits the whole runnable command, so a truncated-diff finder cannot review files outside the target.

findings.claim: `prUrl` is taken only from the metadata payload, so when the metadata read fails but the head bracket verifies the patch, the verified OID is pinned while the PR URL is lost.
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts::a verified head is pinned when only the metadata read fails
findings.reason: The head bracket carries the PR URL as well as the head, so a verified patch can still resolve its repository when metadata fails.

findings.claim: The branch path now runs the advisory `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` probe through assertExec, so a timeout/abort of that probe fails an otherwise valid branch review, contradicting the adjacent comment that the ref probe falls back instead of failing (and differing from the deliberately un-asserted `fullRef`).
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts::a timed-out current-branch probe skips worktree inclusion
findings.reason: The current-branch probe is advisory; a timeout skips worktree inclusion instead of failing the committed range review.

findings.claim: The general-comment idempotency scan pages through every issue comment and downloads all bodies before posting, on every `--comment` run that has even one unposted finding.
findings.reason: Accepted: the paginated scan is the only reliable way to find a per-finding marker in an arbitrary earlier comment; a last-page-only check could miss it and post a duplicate. It runs only when findings fail inline. This is the same trade-off accepted in DELTA3-25.

findings.claim: `applyIndexPlan` resolves the index base by guessing from the plan shape and a per-caller flag, so a legitimate zero-based subset that happens to start at 1 is shifted and applied to the wrong survivors.
findings.test: test/engine.test.ts::a contiguous subset with no index 0 falls back instead of guessing
findings.reason: A contiguous 1..k subset without index 0 is ambiguous; the deterministic fallback keeps every survivor instead of merging the wrong pair. Supersedes DELTA2-08.

findings.claim: `refutedDropped` is a strict subset of `dropped`, so every refuted duplicate is added to the sweep's known list twice with conflicting labels.
findings.test: test/engine.test.ts::distinct refuted scenarios both stay in the refuted guard; test/engine.test.ts::a lower-index recheck never presents unverified text as confirmed
findings.reason: Refuted-only copies and dropped duplicates of kept claims are disjoint lists, so the sweep sees each claim once with the right label.

findings.claim: The streaming path's new per-finder dedupe loop re-implements the existing `dedupeBy` helper instead of calling it.
findings.test: test/engine.test.ts (streaming determinism suite)
findings.reason: The streaming per-finder loop uses the shared dedupeBy helper instead of a second implementation.

findings.claim: The new `CorrectnessLens` type is an exact duplicate of the existing `CleanupLens` type declared 12 lines below it.
findings.test: test/prompts.test.ts (prompt assembly suite)
findings.reason: Correctness and cleanup lenses share one PromptLens contract.

findings.claim: `countDistinctPlaceholders` and its `SAMPLE_PLACEHOLDERS` set are dead duplicates of the live `countDistinctivePlaceholders` counter.
findings.test: test/json.test.ts (echo suite)
findings.reason: The unused countDistinctPlaceholders wrapper and its file-inclusive placeholder set were removed.

findings.claim: Every branch-target review spawns `git rev-parse --symbolic-full-name` even though the result is only consumed when the simple branch-name comparison fails and the ref is remote-tracking.
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts (branch/remote-target suite)
findings.reason: The symbolic-full-name probe is lazy and runs only when the abbreviated comparison fails.

findings.claim: The new general-comment messages rebuild `pluralize` inline with `${n} ${pluralWord(n, ...)}` instead of using the existing `pluralize` helper.
findings.test: test/finding.test.ts::pluralize includes the count while pluralWord does not
findings.reason: The general-comment messages use the shared pluralize helper.

findings.claim: `dedupeVerified` is wired only into the streaming branch, while the barrier path still discards cross-finder duplicates before verification, so the root cause it fixes (a refuted copy suppressing a confirmable duplicate) remains on every non-streaming cell.
findings.test: test/engine.test.ts::a refuted barrier duplicate gets one retry
findings.reason: The barrier path verifies one exact duplicate when its representative is refuted, so a bad first verdict does not discard a confirmable bug.

findings.claim: The summary-comment dedupe only scans general (issue) comments, so a finding already posted inline can be posted again in a general comment when a later run's inline post fails.
findings.test: test/comment.test.ts::an existing inline marker prevents a duplicate general comment
findings.reason: Inline bodies carry the per-finding marker and the general-comment guard scans both inline and general comments.

findings.claim: A head mismatch re-downloads the entire PR patch plus the big metadata payload instead of keeping the already-captured patch and leaving the head unverified.
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts::a moved head keeps the captured patch and leaves the head unverified
findings.reason: A moved head keeps the already-captured patch and leaves the head unverified instead of re-downloading the patch.

findings.claim: The two head-only reads each retry a failed `gh pr view --json headRefOid`, so a host that cannot answer that field pays up to four failing gh invocations before and after the patch download.
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts::a persistent head probe failure is not retried
findings.reason: Only a transient head-read failure is retried; auth/unknown-field errors fall through to the unverified-head fallback.

findings.claim: `CONTROL_CHARS` re-declares the control-character class that `renderPath` in finding.ts already owns.
findings.test: test/scope.test.ts (path/range deny suite)
findings.reason: isShellDenied derives the control-character check from renderPath and the deny substrings from the shared glob list.

findings.claim: String.replace() on text.replace(BLOCK, replacement) interprets `$`-patterns in the replacement, so policy resources containing `$` sequences can be silently mangled during sync.
findings.test: test/agent-policy.test.ts::the policy block replacement writes dollar patterns verbatim
findings.reason: The policy block is replaced with a function replacer, so $ patterns are written literally.

findings.claim: The fallback permission table is generated by `scripts/sync-agent-policy.ts` but nothing runs it or checks it, and the fallback was changed from shell-free to the full shell allowlist, so a host without `agent.transform` relies on a stale hand-committed copy for its read-only guarantees.
findings.test: test/agent-policy.test.ts::the agent-policy sync check passes
findings.reason: The sync script has a --check mode and a test runs it; this was already fixed in f5d68ed.

findings.claim: AGENT_IDS includes `synthesize`, but REVIEW_AGENT_IDS is derived from ROLE_TOOLS, which omits it, so the module's stated invariant (the policy installer patches these IDs, so a rename cannot leave one side pointing at an agent the other never uses) does not hold for the synthesizer.
findings.test: test/agent-policy.test.ts::every agent id names a Markdown agent file
findings.reason: The agent-id comment now states the synthesizer's policy lives in its Markdown file, and a test checks every AGENT_IDS entry names an existing file.

findings.claim: `buildGitHubSummaryArgs` copies the hostname/`gh api` argv preamble from the existing `buildGitHubCommentArgs` builder.
findings.test: test/comment.test.ts (comment builder suite)
findings.reason: The inline and summary builders share one ghApiArgs preamble.
